decision: HOLD stage2 operation pending correction and independent review of exceptional direct-child cleanup.

findings.problem: Exceptional polling/wait failures or KeyboardInterrupt send TERM but allow only two seconds to reap the direct canonical child, then re-raise even when it remains alive. This is shorter than the admitted canonical cleanup reserve and releases wrapper ownership before canonical cleanup completes. The normal timeout path has the intended 15-second allowance.
findings.reproduction: A synthetic wait observer raises once while a reviewer-owned real child is ready. The child cooperatively handles TERM with three seconds of cleanup. The wrapper raises after 2.018 seconds with its direct child still alive. Reviewer subsequently waited and reaped that exact child with exit zero. A second purely synthetic process model corroborates no reaping occurs.
findings.required_fix: Use one bounded exact-direct-child cleanup path for exceptions as well as normal expiry, allowing the remaining canonical cleanup reserve inside the inclusive deadline. Preserve failure evidence, never claim success after an exception, and explicitly record failure if reaping cannot be established. Keep any fallback signal confined to the owned live Popen object; do not scan ancestry, signal unowned groups, or import private canonical APIs. Add real synthetic regression that needs more than two seconds of cooperative cleanup and verifies wrapper does not return while its owned child remains live.
